parallel.requirements: Recognized the sqlparse 0.5.4.dev0 target, official tests, packaging expectations, CLI behavior, examples, and additional spec surface such as config dataclasses and format_sql.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent owned the implementation and delivery path, then delegated a read-only workflow audit by API dimension after the package already passed local checks.
parallel.implementation: Extracted upstream target source/tests, cleaned non-spec files, fixed pyproject/editable installation, added formatter config dataclasses, format_sql, re-exports, examples package, and root conftest.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Submitted a populated workspace containing sqlparse modules, tests, fixtures, examples, packaging files, and helper conftest; no child wrote shared implementation files.
parallel.verification: Ran upstream tests repeatedly, cross-version checks, flake8, CLI/package/import checks, and official evaluation later passed 461 of 461 tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The post-build audit workflow had some in-progress verifier children at timeout, but no required implementation or delivery step remained unfinished for the official outcome.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same sqlparse task, version window, upstream tests, and need to implement a package compatible with the official suite.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Worked entirely as one serial parent because workflows and delegation tools were disabled; chose to implement from scratch after using upstream only for tests and boilerplate.
serial.implementation: Downloaded/cloned upstream, extracted tests and boilerplate, purged upstream implementation/cache, then spent remaining trajectory reading tests and fixtures without creating replacement source files.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No final package tree was assembled; artifact validation copied an empty file list for submission.
serial.verification: Read test files in detail but did not run a completed implementation through the suite; official evaluation completed with zero passed checks.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt timed out with implementation absent and artifact_ok false, causing the official 0/461 result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parallel run recognized the sqlparse task, official 461-check target, and upstream test-suite acceptance bar, then used the target version window to choose source and tests.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had the same prompt and task metadata and also fetched upstream/tests, but it converted that understanding into study rather than a delivered implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had access to the same requirements; the difference is that parallel turned them into a concrete target-source implementation while serial remained in requirement/test analysis.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent owned implementation, packaging, assembly, and delivery, and used the workflow only as a later read-only audit of already-green work.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: With workflow/delegation disabled, the serial parent owned all work but chose a from-scratch plan and did not complete implementation within the budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel centralized the required build path before fan-out; serial centralized ownership too but spent the available window on exploration without creating the package.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow child briefs were bounded read-only audit dimensions with explicit rules to avoid editing and to compare against the current passing upstream test suite.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-interface contracts because delegation was disabled; its context accumulation stayed local in the main trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No parallel interface handoff controlled required implementation. The only child contracts were audit instructions after a package was already assembled.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel extracted the chosen target source tree, verified upstream tests, fixed packaging, added spec extras such as config dataclasses, format_sql, re-exports, and examples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial extracted boilerplate and tests but deleted upstream implementation/cache and did not write replacement sqlparse source before timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered a concrete library implementation; serial left the submitted artifact without implementation files.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel promoted a complete workspace artifact and the status record copied a populated final tree despite the agent process ending by timeout.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial never produced a candidate implementation to promote; its artifact copy succeeded but the submitted file list was empty.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a deliverable before closure; serial had only investigative state and no deliverable candidate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel integrated source, tests, packaging, root conftest, CLI, examples, filters, engine, and package modules in one submitted workspace with no protocol contamination hits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child/shared-write path and no integration conflicts, but also no final source tree to integrate.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant shared-state difference is successful final-tree assembly in parallel versus absent serial assembly, not a parallel write collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran the upstream suite repeatedly, lint/package/import checks, and then passed the official 461-test evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial inspected tests but ran no completed implementation against them, and the official evaluation passed zero of 461 checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had both local and official whole-task acceptance evidence; serial had only test reading and official failure of an empty artifact.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel timed out after launching an optional broad audit workflow, but the artifact had already been built, verified, and copied for official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out, but its budget was consumed by environment setup, upstream/test extraction, and test reading before any implementation was delivered.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Timeout had different closure consequences: harmless for parallel deliverable quality, fatal for serial because no artifact contents existed.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The parallel-only pass is explained by a concrete deliverable difference. Parallel used upstream version analysis to place a complete sqlparse source/test workspace, added required packaging and convenience API extras, verified locally, and submitted a populated artifact that passed the official evaluator. Serial studied the same task and tests but deleted the upstream implementation and did not create a replacement package before timeout, so the submitted artifact was empty and failed official evaluation. The parallel workflow fan-out was broad and unfinished, but it was launched after the artifact was already green and did not create a realized adverse process consequence.
parallel_contributors: Targeted extraction of a compatible upstream 0.5.4.dev0 source tree and official tests.
Parent-owned additive packaging/API/example edits followed by repeated whole-suite and import/CLI verification.
Successful artifact copy and official 461/461 evaluation despite process timeout.
serial_contributors: From-scratch implementation plan after purging upstream source.
Budget spent reading tests and fixtures without writing replacement implementation files.
Empty submitted artifact and official 0/461 evaluation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel reused known-good upstream implementation plus focused additive changes; serial attempted to recreate a large parser library from scratch and did not reach implementation.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause; no retained parallel-side adverse coordination pattern

candidates.reason: Reject: the parallel parent directly owned and performed implementation by extracting the target source, editing formatter and root APIs, and submitting source files before the audit workflow.
Reject: there were no separately delegated implementation components needing reconciliation; the parent integrated source, tests, package config, root conftest, and examples itself.
Reject: the parent assembled the final workspace and status shows a populated copied artifact, so final packaging and placement were owned.
Reject: the parent carried the end-to-end pipeline from source selection through tests, lint, packaging checks, artifact copy, and official evaluation.
Reject: implementation was not blocked behind a child preflight; the workflow audit began only after local tests and package checks were already green.
Reject: parallel investigation did not defer productive implementation; the broad read-only audit was a post-build verification layer, not a first phase that constrained later build work.
Reject: no indispensable implementation or delivery path lacked capacity in parallel; the complete artifact existed before the auxiliary audit consumed remaining time.
Reject: the workflow fan-out was broad and unfinished, but it did not exhaust budget before required implementation, packaging, or official acceptance were achieved.
Reject: no single overbroad child owned indispensable work; child scopes were read-only audit/verifier checks and the parent-owned implementation already passed.
Reject: child briefs were audit-only and stated read-only, empirical, test-bar constraints; no child produced unusable required implementation due to a missing known requirement.
Reject: there were no independently implemented components expected to interoperate across agents, so no missing file/API/interface contract caused incompatibility.
Reject: no known requirement or checkpoint disappeared in transfer and caused repeated work or wrong integration; parent had already validated the artifact locally.
Reject: child audit reports were sometimes long or unfinished, but no required dependent integration was left undone because an available handoff was too bulky to consume.
Reject: no parent action consumed a superseded child report or outdated workspace state in a way that caused rework or invalid verification.
Reject: audit findings included spec-fiction and low-risk suggestions, but no incompatible returned contracts remained unadjudicated and blocked integration.
Reject: the parent had whole-task local test, lint, import, packaging, and later official pass evidence; completion was not based only on child output or file existence.
Reject: the parallel trajectory did not replace or retry a child without inherited findings in a way that repeated required work or consumed needed budget.

candidates.reason: Reject: the overall process timed out with some verifier/audit work in progress, but those children did not own needed deliverable work and no required child result was cut off before implementation.
Reject: the complete candidate was finalized and copied before closure; there was no ready implementation left unpromoted.
Reject: the parent re-ran full tests, lint, and import checks after its implementation edits; no child implementation was merged only after the relevant verification.
Reject: no delegated implementation result existed that the parent failed to retrieve or integrate; the workflow was explicitly read-only audit work.
Reject: some verifier children were still in progress at timeout, but no concrete verifier finding required for delivery was trapped below the parent or caused a wrong final action.
Reject: no required child failed or was cancelled while owning unfinished implementation scope; the parent already completed the work itself.
Reject: no completed child result that contradicted or was necessary to the final decision was ignored; returned audit findings were inspected or harmless to the passing artifact.
Reject: the parent polled workflow progress and continued local verification; it did not simply wait to timeout while actionable required results were available.
Reject: child agents were read-only auditors, so no concurrent agents wrote competing files or behavior claims requiring reconciliation.
Reject: no two live agents edited the same file; the only implementation edits were parent-owned.
Reject: no agent overwrote source produced or owned by another concurrent actor; the parent controlled the source tree.
Reject: no concurrent actor replaced the submitted entry point or artifact while another owned or used it.
Reject: the final workspace was not broadly rebuilt over another agent final tree; copied artifact contents reflect parent-owned assembly.
Reject: workflow agents were instructed read-only and no unstable provenance or shared-write problem is visible.
Reject: no temporary file, cache, or child-generated artifact was consumed as stable reference input by another concurrent actor; protocol shows no contamination hits.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: The broad post-build audit timeout was considered across Load Imbalance, result timing, failure takeover, and monitoring labels, but it had no realized adverse process consequence on required implementation or delivery.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; no candidate clears the realized-adverse-consequence gate for the successful parallel run.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: No labels were retained to avoid converting harmless optional audit fan-out, ordinary timeout metadata, or serial non-delivery into a parallel concurrency error.
